text: When a family wants a medicine mailed instead of handed over, set it up right on the visit's checkout. Nobody re-types the order.
We're at checkout for Juniper's visit.
To mail a medicine, choose Mail order on its line. The mail queue does the rest.
Add the medicine as usual.
Here, Juniper's heartworm chewable.
The line opens, and a prescription needs directions first.
The doctor writes the directions,
the refills,
and whether it's acute or chronic.
Then approves the script. The line closes when it's ready.
Open it again.
Instead of dispense at visit, choose Mail order.
Ship it, or pick it up at an office.
Usually, take payment now with the rest of the visit. The doctor can also approve first, or it can go without payment.
Add it to the mail queue.
The line is tagged Mail order, and shipping is on the bill.
You don't pick a lot. The mail team picks it when they fill the order.
Then check out as usual.
The most common mistakes: dispensing at the visit and then mailing a second one, and picking a lot for a mailed item.
Remember: in the medicine's line on checkout, choose Mail order, and the mail queue does the rest.
